title: Server rejected the CLIENT certificate (EAP-TLS): issuer not trusted
plain_english: This is the mirror image of the usual 'unknown CA' failure: the alert was written by the server, not read from the client. The device presented a certificate whose chain the RADIUS server cannot verify against its ca_file, so the server aborted the handshake. The device may be perfectly fine; the server's trust store is what decides.

causes.cause: ca_file does not contain the CA that issued the client certificates, or is missing an intermediate in that chain.
causes.next_check: On the server: openssl verify -CAfile <ca_file from mods-available/eap> <client cert>; ca_file must hold the root and every intermediate, concatenated.

causes.cause: Devices enrolled from a different CA than the server was set up for (a new PKI, Intune/SCEP, a cloud CA).
causes.next_check: On a failing device, read the client certificate's issuer chain and compare it with the CAs in ca_file.

causes.cause: The client sends only its leaf certificate and the server has no copy of the intermediate to complete the chain.
causes.next_check: Add the intermediate CA certificates to ca_file, or configure the client to send its full chain.
